verdict.rationale: Gmail's own docs describe search operators that filter results, can be combined for narrower results, and can turn a search into a filter; search also works offline. A community user reports searching a large archive easily. Missing for 10: evidence of ranked/relevance-ordered results, evidence of search speed, explicit coverage of the full mail history, and in-depth independent hands-on corroboration of precision.

support.subject: As a power-user, search is fast and precise — operators, filters, and ranked results across my full mail history

citations.quote: You can use words or symbols called search operators to filter your Gmail search results. You can also combine operators to filter your results even more.
After you search, you can use the results to set up a filter for these messages.
You can use Gmail offline to read, search, and reply to messages without an internet connection.
To search for snoozed emails, at the top, in the search bar, enter `in:snoozed`.
